Data.title: Michael Saylor Issues New Bitcoin Buy Signal! Strategy May Buy BTC Again After a Five-Week Break!
Data.body: Strategy founder and Chairman Michael Saylor’s recent social media post has fueled expectations that the company may be preparing to buy Bitcoin again after a long hiatus. Saylor, who shares a chart every Sunday showing the company’s Bitcoin purchases, this time attracted investors’ attention by posting it with the note “Bitcoin Drive engaged.” Market participants are speculating that this post could be an indirect message suggesting Strategy may announce a new Bitcoin purchase on Monday. The company hasn’t announced a new Bitcoin purchase in the past five weeks. This situation stands out as unusual for Strategy, which is known for its regular BTC purchases. Following Saylor’s “We’re gonna need another color” message last week, the company announced on July 27 that it had not purchased any new Bitcoin. According to a recent filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Strategy held 843,775 BTC as of July 26. The company acquired these assets for a total of $63.69 billion, at an average cost of $75,476 per Bitcoin. At current prices, with Bitcoin trading at around $63,200, the company’s Bitcoin portfolio is valued at approximately $53.3 billion, while the cost of the position is estimated to be around $10.4 billion below its actual value. Strategy’s last Bitcoin purchase took place on June 22nd, when the company bought 520 BTC for approximately $34.9 million. However, between June 29th and July 5th, it sold 3,588 BTC to raise approximately $216 million in cash to finance preferred stock payments and strengthen its dollar reserves. Over the past five weeks, the company has not only halted Bitcoin purchases but also increased its dollar reserves to $3.75 billion through common stock sales and initiated a buyback program for STRC shares. These strategic moves have received support from analysts at TD Cowen and Benchmark. *This is not investment advice. Continue Reading: Michael Saylor Issues New Bitcoin Buy Signal! Strategy May Buy BTC Again After a Five-Week Break!

Data.title: Pi Network (PI) Rally Fades, Bitcoin (BTC) Loses $63K: Market Watch
Data.body: The Sunday morning minor relief rally couldn’t continue for long, and bitcoin dived below $63,000 again on Monday and even dipped to $62,200 for the second time in just a few days. The larger-cap alts have joined the ride, with ETH sliding below $1,850, and XRP heading towards a familiar support level. BTC Dips Toward $62K The previous business week began on a significantly more positive note, with BTC defending the $64,000 support and jumping to $65,600 on a couple of occasions. However, the second rejection was quite painful, pushing the cryptocurrency to under $62,800 just a day before the FOMC meeting. Bitcoin’s volatility intensified in the hours before and after the event, in which the Fed ultimately maintained the rates unchanged, despite numerous calls for a hike. BTC jumped on Friday morning once again, reaching $65,400, where the bears stepped up a lot more viciously and drove it south hard. In the following hours, the asset lost roughly three grand and dropped to $62,400. It rebounded to $63,000 on Saturday but dipped to $62,200 later that day. US President Trump’s canceled attacks against Iran and the promise of a new deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz brought a relief rally on Sunday morning, but BTC was halted at $63,700. The leg down on Monday was also unfavorable for the bulls, driving the cryptocurrency south to $62,200 once again. Although that level has stopped the free-fall, BTC remains over 4% down weekly. Its market cap has tumbled to $1.250 trillion, while its dominance over the alts is below 56.5% on CG. BTCUSD August 3. Source: TradingView Alts Back in Red Ethereum was rejected at $1,980 during the July rally, and now struggles below $1,850 after another minor daily decline. XRP fights to stay above $1.05, a support level that was categorized as its ‘battlefield.’ If held, the token still has the chance for a major rebound, analysts asserted. SOL, DOGE, RAIN, ADA, and XMR are also in the red, while HYPE and BNB have posted insignificant gains. Pi Network’s PI impressed over the weekend, posting some notable gains of 5-6% even as the market stalled. Today, though, its progress has stalled, and the asset is down over 5% to under $0.084. MemeCore and Algorand are among the few alts in the green daily, while BEAT has plunged by 24%, followed by ONDO’s 6% crash. The total crypto market cap has shed around $40 billion in a day and is down to $2.220 trillion on CG. Cryptocurrency Market Overview August 3. Data.title: Ripple Positions XRP Ledger as the Backbone of Next-Generation Capital Markets Through Strategic ZILO & Liquido Investments
Data.body: Ripple Strengthens XRPL for Institutional Finance With Strategic ZILO and Licuido Deals Ripple is accelerating its push into global capital markets with strategic investments in ZILO and Licuido, expanding the institutional infrastructure underpinning the XRP Ledger (XRPL) . More notably, these additions bring regulated transfer agency , digital asset issuance, and collateral mobility to Ripple's ecosystem, underscoring its ambition to become a leading provider of infrastructure for tokenized finance, not just cross-border payments. The announcement comes shortly after Aviva Investors tokenized its U.S. Dollar Liquidity Fund on the XRPL, signaling that institutional adoption is moving beyond pilot programs into real-world deployment. It also follows reports that Ripple's valuation has climbed to $50 billion, highlighting growing confidence in its expanding role across digital finance. Ripple believes tokenization is only the starting point. The greater opportunity lies in enabling tokenized assets to be traded, financed, pledged as collateral, and settled instantly within a regulated ecosystem, replacing slow and fragmented legacy processes. Ripple's Capital Markets Vision Takes Shape With Institutional-Grade XRPL Infrastructure Despite rapid innovation, global capital markets still rely on infrastructure built decades ago, where settlement can take days and trillions of dollars in collateral remain locked up. Ripple aims to modernize this system by building an end-to-end investment infrastructure on the XRPL. Its institutional platform combines token issuance, secure custody, collateral management, multi-currency investment capabilities, and atomic settlement. RLUSD, Ripple's U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin, acts as the regulated settlement asset for delivery-versus-payment transactions, enabling tokenized assets to be used as collateral immediately while reducing counterparty risk through simultaneous settlement. Therefore, these investments reinforce this strategy from two key fronts. ZILO provides regulated transfer agency and fund administration technology, giving asset managers and custodians the compliant ownership records and operational infrastructure required to support tokenized funds at institutional scale. Licuido extends those capabilities by enabling regulated issuance, distribution, trading, and collateral mobility, allowing tokenized assets to move efficiently across digital markets and unlock liquidity from assets that would otherwise remain idle. Ripple Senior Vice President of Trading and Markets Nigel Khakoo said tokenization alone is not enough, stressing that the real value comes from enabling digital assets to be traded, settled, and deployed as collateral in real time. He cited collaborations with Aviva Investors, Franklin Templeton, and DBS as evidence that major financial institutions are preparing to scale tokenized investment products. ZILO CEO Phil Goffin said Ripple's investment will accelerate the development of compliant infrastructure for tokenized funds, while Licuido CEO Brian Lynch noted that meaningful liquidity depends on assets being able to circulate freely within regulated markets rather than remaining dormant. Why are these investments a game-changer? Well, they deepen Ripple's institutional strategy, positioning the XRPL as a comprehensive capital markets platform rather than simply a network for token issuance. By combining regulated administration, collateral mobility, liquidity, and atomic settlement, Ripple is laying the foundation for a more efficient financial system. This vision is already extending beyond tokenization. Through Ripple Prime , the company is building infrastructure connected to the DTCC ecosystem. With the Fixed Income Clearing Corporation (FICC) processing more than $1.2 trillion in U.S. Treasury transactions each day, Ripple is increasingly positioning the XRPL at the convergence of blockchain innovation and traditional finance, where tokenized assets can be issued, traded, financed, and settled at institutional scale.

Data.title: Stablecoin Yield Now Funds Daily SUI Buybacks
Data.body: There’s a new lever in Sui’s tokenomics toolkit. Stablecoin yield, once a sleepy back-office line item, is now being routed into regular SUI purchases on the open market. The pitch is simple: turn passive dollar yield into steady token demand. This piece breaks down how that actually works, why it matters for SUI’s day-to-day trading dynamics, what could go wrong, and the signs that tell you if the program is doing real work or just headline duty. We’ll keep it practical and grounded in current Sui data, including stablecoin float, throughput experiments, and the supply calendar that makes buybacks matter. In short, yield from stablecoin treasuries and on-chain dollar positions is being allocated to scheduled SUI buy programs that run daily. The idea is to convert interest income into a predictable bid that can offset emissions, smooth unlock weeks, and recycle ecosystem dollars back into the native asset. This isn’t a price guarantee. Size depends on stablecoin balances, interest rates, and transparent execution. What funds it: interest from stablecoin reserves or yield-bearing dollar products held by ecosystem treasuries. Why daily: smaller, frequent TWAP-style buys reduce slippage and front-running risk compared to chunky weekly orders. What it can offset: emissions and unlock-driven supply pressure, at least at the margin. What sets the ceiling: stablecoin float on Sui and prevailing rates. If either falls, buy power shrinks. Core risk: opacity, peg or counterparty risk on the yield source, and assuming a hard price floor that does not exist. Where does the yield actually come from? Two broad buckets. First, fiat-backed stablecoins often park reserves in cash, T-bills, and repos that yield interest. That yield typically accrues to the issuer, not holders, but if a Sui-aligned treasury holds its own stables or uses yield-bearing wrappers, it can capture that interest and redirect it to buybacks. Second, on-chain cash can be deployed into conservative yield products like tokenized T-bills, money-market wrappers , or reputable on-chain credit. The posture here is risk-managed, not degen. If the dollar base is large and rates are decent, the stream is non-trivial. The base on Sui is there. DefiLlama shows Sui’s on-chain stablecoin market cap in the hundreds of millions, roughly 428 million at an Aug 3, 2026 snapshot, which frames the potential pool that could generate reserve yield on Sui itself DefiLlama (Sui chain page) . A single issuer example, USDsui, had a circulating market cap around 71 to 72 million in late July 2026, which is already enough to throw off meaningful interest if put in short-term instruments CoinMarketCap . And the pipes are tested. In a public programmable-tunnels experiment on July 4, 2026, Sui pushed a headline 6,086,766 transactions per second, showing the throughput runway is more than marketing The Cryptonomist . Since August 2025, the network has processed more than one trillion dollars in stablecoin volume, a reminder that dollar rails on Sui are not a rounding error The Cryptonomist . How do daily buybacks run on-chain? Think of it as a slow drip, not a cannon. A treasury wallet accrues dollar yield. A scheduler checks the accrued amount, then routes a pre-set fraction into SUI buys at fixed intervals. Execution should be venue-agnostic and liquidity-aware, so it leans into pools with depth and spreads the flow. Good implementations do three things. One, they disclose the source of funds and the policy that sets size and timing. Two, they publish addresses and a simple dashboard so anyone can verify the buys. Three, they use execution strategies that reduce slippage and minimize MEV exposure. No hero trades, just boring consistency. Checklist for credible buyback ops: Clear policy: target daily notional, caps, and pause conditions. Named wallets with on-chain tagging and regular reports. Execution via TWAP or RFQ across top venues, not a single pool. Audited custody of the yield source, with counterparty lists and limits. Kill switch and incident playbook tested in staging. What changes for SUI’s market structure? Daily buybacks are a microstructure nudge. You introduce a consistent buyer that shows up independent of headlines. That has three knock-on effects. It can tighten spreads during quiet hours, slightly lift baseline depth near mid, and make net flows less lumpy across the week. The timing matters most around supply events. On or around July 3, 2026, a scheduled unlock of 25,666,876 SUI hit the tape, the kind of cliff that reminds you why any counter-flow can matter CryptoDaily . A daily buy program does not erase the unlock, but it can put steady pressure the other way and, more importantly, reduce the incentive for shorts to lean in when they sniff one-way order flow. The backbone for this is a robust dollar rail. With more than a trillion dollars of stablecoin transaction volume since Aug 2025, and a test showing multi-million TPS headroom, Sui has the payment capacity to move stablecoin yield around without clogging user activity The Cryptonomist . Pro tip: focus on size relative to average daily SUI spot volume during calm periods. A program that is 1 to 3 percent of typical daily notional will be felt. Ten basis points, less so. How big could this really be, realistically? It comes down to the math of dollars, rates, and policy. For every 100 million dollars of principal earning 5 percent annually, you generate roughly 13,700 dollars per day per 100 million. If the stablecoin base is higher, or rates are higher, scale up linearly. If rates fall or treasuries sit idle, scale down. Even modest daily notional can be punchy when it is patient and consistent. Markets get used to flow. If the program posts buys across the whole day and steps away during volatility spikes, it can absorb a surprising amount of passive sell pressure without telegraphing itself. Funding modelSource of cashFlow profileProsTrade-offsEmissionsNew token supplyContinuous or scheduledBootstraps growth quicklyDilution, sell pressure, mercenary capitalFee buybacksProtocol revenuesHighly cyclical with usageAligns with economic activityWeak in bear markets, noisyStablecoin-yield buybacksInterest on dollar reservesSmooth, rate-drivenPredictable bid, low headline riskDependent on rates, counterparty/peg risk Note the middle column. Fee buybacks spike when everyone is trading. Stablecoin-yield buybacks are steadier, tied to rates and principal, not your weekend DEX volume. How does this compare to fee buybacks or burns? Burn mechanics retire supply and can be powerful when usage is soaring, but they concentrate impact in hot markets and often go quiet in the cold ones. Fee buybacks are usage-levered too. Stablecoin-yield buybacks decouple a share of the bid from daily protocol activity by leaning on the interest rate cycle and the size of the dollar base. You do not need to pick one. A blended approach tends to be healthier. Use emissions to seed the network. Let fees fund opportunistic buybacks and runway. Let stablecoin yield provide the steady drip. Write policies that can dial each leg up or down as the market changes. What matters more than the verb on the tin, buy or burn, is the audit trail. If the market cannot trace dollars to buys to custody, trust erodes fast. What are the main risks and failure modes? Start with the yield source. If the program leans on fiat-backed stables, you are taking issuer and banking partner risk. If it leans on tokenized T-bills or money market wrappers, you are adding wrapper and custodian risk on top. If it uses on-chain credit, underwrite that like a lender, not a trader. Policy drift is another. Today’s gentle daily TWAP can drift into hero mode during a drawdown, at exactly the wrong time. Keep hard caps and pause rules, and publish them. Then there is execution risk. Poorly designed schedules can telegraph flow and invite front-running. Fragmented liquidity can create slippage that chews through the very yield you are trying to recycle. Warning: buybacks are not a price floor. They are a flow. If the market wants lower, it will go lower. Treat buybacks as a tailwind, not a shield. What should holders and builders watch next? Three buckets. Dollars, rates, and proof. Dollars, meaning the stablecoin float that can earn yield in the first place. DefiLlama’s Sui chain dashboard showed about 428 million in stablecoins at an Aug 3, 2026 snapshot, a rough proxy for how big the well could be if it is actually tapped DefiLlama (Sui chain page) . Rates, because they set the drip rate. If the front end of the curve slides lower, the daily SUI ticket size shrinks, even if the dollar base is steady. If rates rise, you get more breathing room. Proof is the non-negotiable. We should see named buyback wallets, schedules, and weekly recaps that reconcile source yield, executed notional, fees, and custody balances. Bonus points for showing venue breakdown, spread cost, and any rebates captured. Keep one more thing in mind. Sui’s rails are built for this kind of automation. The network’s July 4 test pushed a multi-million TPS headline, and since Aug 2025 it has cleared over a trillion dollars in stablecoin transfers. That foundation makes a daily buyback program logistically boring, which is exactly what you want The Cryptonomist . Common Mistakes Assuming a hard price floor. A steady bid helps, but it does not negate macro drawdowns or supply shocks. Size programs to complement, not replace, risk management. Ignoring the source of yield. If you cannot name the issuer, custodian, and wrapper risks, you are not earning yield, you are borrowing trouble. Under-disclosing mechanics. Without addresses, schedules, and reconciliation, the market will price your buybacks like vapor. Over-sizing in thin markets. Large single-venue orders invite MEV and slippage. Spread and randomize the flow inside clear risk bands. Forgetting the supply calendar. Unlocks, validator rewards, and ecosystem grants all matter. Map the daily buy capacity against known issuance and cliffs. If you want a steady diet of grounded coverage and data-led explainers around these mechanics, you can always find more at Crypto Daily . Frequently Asked Questions Can daily buybacks continue if interest rates fall? Yes, but the ticket size shrinks. Since these programs are funded by interest income, a lower front end of the curve means less daily notional. Good policy frameworks adjust frequency or size rather than force the same spend in a lower-yield regime. Are tokens bought then burned, or held? It depends on the policy. Some programs retire tokens to reduce float. Others hold in treasury to use for grants or liquidity. What matters is disclosure. If it is a burn, publish the burn address. If it is custody, publish the wallets and periodic balances. What if the stablecoin issuer changes terms or suffers a peg wobble? Then the yield source is at risk. Diversify across issuers and wrappers, keep conservative counterparty limits, and maintain a fast switch to cash if thresholds trip. The buyback policy should include explicit triggers to pause when peg or counterparty risk breaches set bands. Could buybacks be gamed or front-run? They can be if you are predictable. Reduce that by splitting orders, randomizing execution windows, using RFQ or private liquidity when appropriate, and monitoring for toxic flow. A public schedule is fine, but do not publish minute-by-minute plans. Is this the same as what other chains did with burns and reserves? Not exactly. Stablecoin-yield buybacks are rate-driven and tend to be smaller and steadier than fee or reserve burns. The cautionary tale is thinking any mechanism can defy gravity. Use this as one leg in a multi-pronged tokenomics framework. How can I verify the daily activity on-chain? Look for tagged treasury and buyback wallets, then follow the transfers into execution venues. Cross-check with a simple community dashboard that lists daily notional, fees, and remaining dry powder. If you cannot verify it, discount it. Do these buybacks help during big unlock weeks? They help at the margin by being a steady counter-flow, but they do not erase unlocks. Around the early July 2026 SUI unlock, for example, what mattered was preparation and liquidity, not heroics on the day CryptoDaily . Treat buybacks as one of several tools alongside grants, market making, and messaging. Disclaimer: This article is provided for informational purposes only. It is not offered or intended to be used as legal, tax, investment, financial, or other advice.

Data.title: Pundit Explains How XRP Could Hit $100, Says XRP Doesn’t Care About Market Cap
Data.body: As conversations surrounding XRP’s long-term value continue, crypto enthusiast Jenny has offered a perspective that focuses on the digital asset’s utility instead of its market capitalization. She believes XRP’s ability to facilitate high-volume financial settlements is a more meaningful measure of its importance than its total market value. Her latest comments explain why she views traditional valuation models as inadequate for an asset built to move liquidity across financial networks. Jenny presented a hypothetical scenario on X in which XRP reaches a price of $100 while maintaining a circulating supply of 50 billion tokens. Under those conditions, XRP’s market capitalization would stand at approximately $5 trillion. She stressed, however, that the figure would not reflect the full scale of value the network could process. XRP doesn't care about market cap. • XRP Price = $100 • Circulating Supply = 50B XRP • Market Cap = $5 trillion • However, if each XRP is used for settlement 1,000 times a day, it could theoretically support a daily flow of $5 quadrillion. So, even with a market cap of $5… pic.twitter.com/gyqZZHcQsK — Jenny (@Jenny_Solstice) August 1, 2026 Repeated Use Could Expand XRP’s Settlement Capacity Jenny explained that if every XRP token were used for settlement 1,000 times each day, the network could theoretically support as much as $5 quadrillion in daily transaction volume. In her view, a payment asset can process value far beyond its market capitalization because the same tokens can be reused continuously rather than remaining idle. She described XRP as infrastructure for transferring liquidity instead of a store of value. From that perspective, network activity, transaction speed, and liquidity efficiency become far more significant than the asset’s market capitalization. To illustrate her point, Jenny compared XRP with SWIFT, noting that the global financial messaging network has no market capitalization despite facilitating trillions of dollars in transactions every day. She used this comparison to suggest that financial infrastructure should not be evaluated solely through market value. Utility Takes Priority Over Market Cap Jenny also stated that XRP serves as a bridge for liquidity in an increasingly tokenized financial system. Because of that role, she believes adoption should be measured by network usage, liquidity speed, and transaction throughput rather than by market capitalization alone. She added that if XRP eventually handles even a small portion of the global derivatives market, traditional market cap calculations would lose much of their relevance. Under such a scenario, the network’s settlement activity would provide a better indication of its value than its circulating market valuation. We are on X, follow us to connect with us :- @TimesTabloid1 — TimesTabloid (@TimesTabloid1) June 15, 2025 Community Members Respond Jenny’s comments drew different reactions from members of the XRP community. Pardeep Singh questioned the likelihood of XRP reaching a $5 trillion market capitalization, saying investors would already consider a price between $6 and $8 to be a major achievement. Another commenter, Keith, focused on the comparison with SWIFT. He noted that SWIFT operates as a messaging network, which is why it does not have a market capitalization. Even so, he added that XRP represents a different type of financial technology and expressed the view that blockchain-based settlement systems could eventually replace older financial infrastructure. Data.title: XRP Ledger Sponsored Fees Proposal Could Make XRP Less Visible To Some Users
Data.body: A proposed XRP Ledger amendment known as XLS-68 could let sponsors cover transaction fees and reserves for other users, making it possible for some wallet interactions to happen without the end user directly holding XRP. The feature, included in the xrpld v3.3.0 amendment bundle, is part of a broader move toward fee abstraction and smoother user onboarding. That does not mean XRP demand will definitely fall. It means some users may be able to interact with applications while another party handles fees and reserves behind the scenes. For apps and wallets , that can make the user experience much simpler. For XRP holders, it raises a more nuanced debate about how fee abstraction affects native-token visibility. TL;DR XLS-68 would allow sponsors to cover fees and reserves for other users. The proposal could make some XRPL interactions possible without users directly holding XRP. This is a UX change, not proof that XRP demand will fall. Why Native Fees Create Friction Most blockchains require users to hold the native asset for transaction fees. That makes sense at the protocol level, but it creates onboarding friction. A new user may receive a stablecoin or token but still need XRP to move it. That adds an extra step, and every extra step loses users. Fee sponsorship tries to solve that. An app, wallet, exchange , business, or other sponsor can cover the fee and reserve requirements, letting the end user interact more smoothly. This is common in broader crypto UX thinking. Many networks are trying to make blockchain fees less visible to mainstream users. XRP Becomes Infrastructure, Not Always A User-Facing Asset If sponsored fees work well, XRP may become less visible in some user journeys. A person using an app may not need to think about acquiring XRP first. The app handles it. That can be good for adoption because it reduces friction, especially for consumer or enterprise products. But it also changes how users perceive the native asset. If users no longer directly hold XRP for every interaction, some traders may wonder whether fee demand weakens. That is the debate around the amendment. The answer is not simple. Sponsors still need a way to fund fees and reserves. Network activity still depends on the ledger’s economics. The question is who holds and spends XRP, not whether the network stops needing it entirely. UX Improvements Can Increase Overall Activity There is another side to the demand argument. If sponsored fees make XRPL easier to use, the network may attract more applications and transactions. More users may interact with apps if they do not need to manage XRP directly on day one. That could offset reduced user-facing fee friction. In other words, XRP might become less visible per user but support more total activity if onboarding improves. That is why it is too simplistic to say sponsored fees are bearish or bullish. The real effect depends on adoption, sponsor behavior, transaction volume, reserve mechanics, and how apps implement the feature. Enterprise Use Cases May Benefit Most Fee abstraction is especially relevant for enterprise and consumer-facing products. A bank, fintech, gaming app, payment company, or stablecoin issuer may not want users dealing with native-token balances just to complete basic actions. Sponsored fees let those companies hide some blockchain complexity while still using XRPL underneath. That can make the ledger more attractive for tokenized asset or payment flows. But again, this only matters if the amendment activates and builders use it. A proposed feature is not adoption. It is infrastructure that may enable adoption. Watch The Vote And Implementation The next step is validator support. Like other XRPL amendments, XLS-68 needs the required consensus threshold before activation. Until then, it remains a proposal in the release path, not a live feature reshaping user behavior. If activated, the market can then watch how wallets and apps integrate it. For now, the sponsored fees proposal is best understood as a UX and fee-abstraction story. It may reduce the need for some users to hold XRP directly, but it could also make XRPL easier to use and expand application activity. The impact depends on what builders do next. This article is based on XRP Ledger amendment materials related to XLS-68 sponsored fees and reserves . This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae. This report is based on information released in disclosures at primary source documentation .

Data.title: Alibaba takes on OpenAI and Anthropic with its biggest AI model yet
Data.body: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. debuted Qwen3.8-Max, its latest AI model, ahead of next week’s planned open-weight release to the public. The new model features 2.4 trillion parameters and outperforms Moonshot’s newly launched Kimi K3 on multiple benchmarks. It also marks the company’s return to its open-source roots after several of its top-tier AI models were launched as proprietary offerings earlier this year. The new model is now available on Alibaba Cloud’s Model Studio APIs and through QwenWork, the company’s AI assistant platform for businesses. Plus, the provider plans to go public next week, handing users the tools to fine-tune the AI themselves. This launch puts Alibaba in fierce competition with rivals, OpenAI and Anthropic. Instead of proprietary AI systems that provide API access only, an open-weight release allows developers and businesses to download the model weights to customize them for their own AI systems and build upon them for their own applications. This will enable businesses to control deployment, privacy, and performance optimization, and researchers can replicate Alibaba’s work without starting from scratch. This also supports Alibaba’s strategic goal of driving enterprise adoption across its AI ecosystem. Qwen3.8-Max excels at processing and autonomous, says Alibaba According to Alibaba, the new model achieved results comparable to—or even better than—Anthropic’s Fable 5 in several benchmarks. It can map complex data, such as video streams and thick manuals, into searchable archives. Moreover, it recreates apps using screenshots, designs interactive games and educational content, and converts flat floor plans into immersive 3D visualizations. The company also noted that the model excels at autonomous coding, complex research, and other tasks that require extended processing. It proved its autonomy by driving an in-house software project solo for 16 days. Additionally, the latest system boosts efficiency by activating only the required parts, helping reduce processing costs and latency. So far, in user-voted arenas, Alibaba’s model has captured top spots, trailing only a few premium Claude models. It secured fifth place in text and second in vision. It initially dropped on July 19 via Alibaba’s subscription plan and Qoder ecosystem. At the time, Alibaba asserted that the system performance was second only to Fable 5. The debut lifted Alibaba’s shares by as much as 7.3%, their best performance in nearly a month. The market reaction suggests investors view AI as one of Alibaba’s key long-term growth drivers. The company has invested heavily in cloud computing and generative AI, with stronger model performance expected to attract more enterprise customers to its cloud services and developer ecosystem. China and US AI rivalry continues The latest launch reflects the increasingly intense competition between Chinese and U.S. AI developers, who are racing to release more capable foundation models at a faster pace. Rather than competing solely on benchmark scores, companies are now differentiating themselves through coding performance, multimodal capabilities, enterprise adoption, and the availability of open-source models that developers can freely customize. The latest Qwen debut adds momentum to China’s rapid catch-up, arriving days after Moonshot’s Kimi stunned Western tech hubs. Chinese labs are still fighting to eclipse OpenAI and Anthropic using fractionally fewer computing resources. For starters, DeepSeek just expanded its V4 Flash access while ByteDance and MiniMax launched video models on Friday. Vey-Sern Ling, managing director at Union Bancaire Privée, even argued that the Chinese models are growing increasingly close in performance with other US superior models. He contended, “Many investors continue to underestimate Chinese AI models because of US chip restrictions or general skepticism. In reality, the gap is probably much closer and narrowing fast. Alibaba’s Qwen 3.8 is another proof point, following Kimi K3.” Though over the last few months, the rivalry between the two countries has intensified. Earlier, the US government blacklisted foreign access to Anthropic’s Fable 5 and Mythos 5 . The government temporarily restricted the models as a precaution to prevent security bypassing by Chinese authorities. Nonetheless, on Washington’s order, Anthropic returned access to its overseas base. It noted, however, that it was instituting stronger safeguards to protect its technology and had made commitments to the government. More recently, the firm also accused Chinese developers of distillation attacks. The San Francisco-based company told two U.S. lawmakers in a letter that operators associated with Alibaba used thousands of fake accounts to conduct nearly 29 million exchanges with Claude, calling it the biggest extraction campaign it has seen. The AI startup even urged lawmakers to hold companies behind these attacks accountable and reinforce measures to prevent U.S. technology from being stolen. The exploit was highly selective, focusing on Claude’s knack for managing intricate projects and high-level reasoning, according to the San Francisco-based company. Data.title: Important Ripple (XRP) Announcement, New Investments: August 3
Data.body: Ripple has expanded its digital capital markets strategy. The company announced today investments in Zilo and Lucuido – two firms that are focused on developing infrastructure for tokenized funds and institutional asset trading. The move builds on existing partnerships with both firms. Ripple did not disclose the size of either investment. Speaking on the matter was Nigel Khakoo, SVP, Trading and Markets at Ripple, who said: “… ZILO and Licuido provide core capabilities that are essential to further scaling this shift: regulated digital transfer agency infrastructure and liquidity for issuance and collateral mobility. This is just the beginning of the journey, and we see a substantial opportunity to bring huge efficiencies to the investment sector over the next decade.” ZILO provides transfer agency and fund administration technology. Its systems give asset managers and custodians regulated digital records for tokenized share classes. Licuido, on the other hand, operates an FCA-regulated platform that supports the issuance, distribution, trading, and use of traditional assets as digital collateral. Ripple plans to integrate these capabilities with its infrastructure on the XRP Ledger. The company wants institutions to issue tokenized assets, hold them in custody, move them between investors, and use them as collateral without relying on legacy systems. Naturally, RLUSD will serve as the regulated cash component for delivery-versus-payment transactions. This structure is designed to allow the asset and payment sides of a trade to settle together on XRPL. The investments also support Ripple’s recent push to build a broader institutional platform around tokenization, payments, stablecoins, and trading. Last month, the firm launched Ripple Mint and made an investment in compliance provider Notabene. This strengthens the infrastructure that’s available to institutions using RLUSD. It’s also noteworthy that the company has worked with Aviva Investors, Franklin Templeton, and DBS on tokenized fund and collateral projects. Ripple said that ZILO and Licuido will help turn those individual partnerships into infrastructure that asset managers can use at scale. Data.title: Dormant whale moves $1 billion in Bitcoin as market sits 50% below peak
Data.body: A lone Bitcoin transaction has ended a prolonged period of silence lasting seven months. According to blockchain tracker Lookonchain, a wallet containing 16,400 BTC , equivalent to $1.04 billion, made the transfer of its whole balance on August 3. This transfer coincides with the price of Bitcoin being approximately $62,800, which is almost 50 percent lower than its October 2025 record of $126,198, making such billion-dollar transfers by big players a noteworthy moment in the industry. The key question is not whether or not the coins have transferred locations, but rather their future direction. On-chain data does not show evidence that the Bitcoin was sent to an established exchange, meaning that this may actually be a custody reshuffle instead of a preparation for a sale. A wallet quiet since the start of the year empties in one move The issuing wallet, bc1qptc9cz269u2mc5yguun5a5d6yd5c7f7ne4qj26, has not been used for approximately seven months until it transferred all its balance to a new recipient wallet: bc1qyt5gsrxp553v9fuwk8gugv… The transaction transferred exactly 16,400 BTC, worth about $1.04 billion when it was executed. As reported by Cypher Citadel, the transaction stands out as one of the largest 0.01% of all crypto exchanges during the past three-month period and accounts for about 0.0781% of the total Bitcoin supply of 21 million coins. According to the analytics platform, the transaction is classified as an unknown-to-unknown wallet transfer, a type of transaction typically associated with internal custody reshuffling or over-the-counter transactions instead of deposits to exchanges. The transaction authenticity can be confirmed independently using blockchain explorers: Arkham Intelligence: https://arkm.com/explorer/address/bc1qptc9cz269u2mc5yguun5a5d6yd5c7f7ne4qj26 mempool.space : https://mempool.space/address/bc1qptc9cz269u2mc5yguun5a5d6yd5c7f7ne4qj26 Transaction hash: db270f…7939 (full hash available on mempool.space ) Bitcoin is near $62,800 and lower this week The timing of this transaction played a big role in its meaning. According to CryptoQuant, the price of Bitcoin on the day of the transaction was about $62,808, which was a 1.1% drop in 24 hours and a 3.8% decrease for the last week. CoinMarketCap stated that the spot exchange price was about $62,768 and that the volume of the spot exchange for the last 24 hours was almost $15.7 billion. In light of that, the transfer of $1.04 billion amounts to approximately 6% to 7% of a regular day’s reported spot amount. This is sufficiently significant to raise eyebrows; on the other hand, it may not be “big” enough to have any impact on the market, unless the tokens find their way to exchanges’ order books. The raw amount of the transaction tells only a small part of the story. While 16,400 BTC accounts for just 0.0781% of the total Bitcoin available in circulation, it represents a much larger proportion of Bitcoin in circulation that is actually available for trading. It is believed that millions of Bitcoins have been lost and permanently kept by long-term investors, thereby reducing the liquid Bitcoin supply for trading transactions. This is the reason why people focus less on the size of the Bitcoin transferred and more on whether the coins end up deposited into exchange addresses. A new wallet—not an exchange As of now, the location of the coins is shedding the most light on the matter. Data from the blockchain reveals that the Bitcoin was sent to a wallet created specifically for this transfer rather than being sent to a known exchange address. Cypher Citadel confirmed that the nature of the trade was, in isolation, neutral, because there seems to be no known exchange presence at either end of the transaction. The firm stressed that the next window of 4 to 48 hours will be a key timeframe to look for follow-up transactions into centralized exchanges, where actual selling pressure can be expected. In July, a Bitcoin wallet that had not been active for over eight years sent 5,907.56 BTC (equivalent to around $384 million) to another wallet address without transferring the assets to a cryptocurrency exchange. Blockchain analytics firm Glassnode notes that transfers between two wallets can indicate changes in custody , cold storage, or the process of managing funds internally between wallets. Wallet transfers to exchanges, on the other hand, are considered to be an indication that the owners might intend to sell their Bitcoins. A larger example occurred earlier in 2025 when around 80,000 BTC that had been dormant since Satoshi’s time —valued at roughly $8 billion—was transferred for the first time in close to 14 years. Yet the transaction did not bring about an immediate flow of funds into exchanges. So far, this billion-dollar deal follows the same trend. Until there are further transactions on the blockchain that indicate otherwise, it appears that the coins might be moving into new wallets rather than finding themselves ready for sale. The blockchain has already logged the transaction of $1 billion worth of Bitcoins, but they have yet to indicate that the coins are headed for exchange wallets.
